semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: 'Pre-training techniques' and 'pre-training' share nearly identical meanings. Both refer to methodologies applied prior to primary model training, emphasizing feature extraction and model initialization.

parent_domains.justification: 'Training' is a broad term encompassing all forms of strengthening a model's performance, including 'pre-training techniques.'
'Optimization and training' is a macro view that contains various stages and facets, including 'pre-training techniques,' within its fold.

closest_parent_domain.justification: 'Training' is the general category under which 'pre-training techniques' precisely falls since pre-training is a subset or a stage of training.

child_domains.justification: 'Contrastive pretraining' is a more specific method under 'pre-training techniques,' focusing on leveraging contrastive learning principles.

'Language model pre-training' zooms in on applying pre-training techniques specifically within language models, highlighting a specific application area of the generally broader 'pre-training techniques.'
'Image-text pretraining' details the use of pre-training techniques where both image and text data are involved, showing an application-based narrower focus.

closest_child_domain.justification: 'Language model pre-training' is most recognized and popular within the breadth of pre-training techniques, often serving as a common reference or entry point into understanding the practical implementations of pre-training.

sibling_domains.justification: 'Retraining' shares the same broad 'training' parent domain but focuses on the aspects of reintroducing trained data for performance improvement.
'Network training' operates under 'training' but involves different methodologies beyond mere pre-initialization.
'Communication-efficient training' aligns under the broad domain but emphasizes strategies to reduce data communication during the training phase.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: 'Retraining' is intimately connected with pre-training stages as both involve phases of the training process to refine model performance, often discussed together in deep learning strategies.

unrelated_domains.justification: 'Non-technical skills training' is unrelated as it deals with skill-building outside of the technical computations of deep learning.
'Motor learning' focuses more on physiological and biomechanical skills, different from the computational focus of pre-training.
Even though broadly associated, 'learning theory' is more foundational and theoretical compared to the practical aspect of 'pre-training techniques.'
